title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). M is a set of 'pieces' X. Each piece has a boundary ∂X and is ordered by relations ≪, ≤ and |∘| (|∘| means 'interiors disjoint'). For X in M, X̃ is the set of 'elementary' sub-pieces of X. It plays the role of the face poset of a cell decomposition of X, and Ỹ ⊂ X̃ is read as the set of faces of Y.

Grothendieck wants a support function X ↦ |X| ∈ 𝔓(P), where P is a set of 'points'. Its axioms are:
(i) |X| is monotone for ≪ (hence for ≤);
(ii) the open part |X|° := |X| \ |∂X| is non-empty;
(iii) X |∘| Y ⇔ |X|° ∩ |Y|° = ∅;
(iv) normalisation: |M| = P and the |X|° separate points.
On the previous page he strengthened (ii) to (ii bis): the |Y|, Y ∈ X̃, form the cellular decomposition of |X| induced by X. He also deduced that Y ↦ |Y| is injective on X̃.

This page.
1. He asks whether, for Y, Z ∈ X̃, |Y| ⊂ |Z| ⇒ Y ≤ Z. In other words: is the order on X̃ the one induced by inclusion in 𝔓(P)? He notes this does not follow from (i)–(iv). It might be implicit in the words 'indexed by X̃' (indexed as an ordered set) in (ii bis), but he wants a proof.
2. A preliminary is needed: the open part |Y|° should be intrinsically defined from the decomposition. He defines |Y|°′ := |Y| \ ⋃{|Z| : Z ∈ X̃, |Z| ⊊ |Y|} and asks whether |Y|° = |Y|°′. He worries the union might contain Z that are not < Y.
3. Argument for equality. By (ii bis) the |Y| cover |X|. Taking, for a point x, a minimal |Y| containing it (implicitly X̃ finite or well-founded), the |Y|°′ cover |X|. Combined with |Y|°′ ⊂ |Y|°, the |Y|° also cover. By (iii) the |Y|° are pairwise disjoint. Hence |Y|° = |Y|°′, and |X| = ⨆_{Y∈X̃} |Y|°, a partition into open cells (later called (ii ter)).
4. He returns to the question, introducing L = Ỹ ∩ Z̃ and Ỹ ∪ Z̃. The next page finishes it: |Y| ∩ |Z| = ⋃_{T∈L} |T|°. So |Y| ⊂ |Z| forces Ỹ \ L = ∅, i.e. Y ≤ Z, since the open cells are non-empty.

Modern meaning. For a 'regular cell complex'-type structure, each closed cell is the disjoint union of the open cells of its faces. The face poset is recovered as the inclusion order of closed cells (the frontier/closure condition). This is a step in an axiomatic, point-set realisation of the combinatorial 'tame topology' Grothendieck was developing in the Analysis situs manuscripts.
errors: The inclusion |Y|°′ ⊂ |Y|° is used tacitly. It needs |∂Y| ⊂ ⋃_{Z<Y}|Z| plus |Z| ⊊ |Y| for Z < Y; the latter follows from injectivity and monotonicity, the former presumably from (ii bis) applied to Y. Grothendieck himself notes on the next page that (ii bis) is used for Y and Z, not only X.
The claim that the |Y|°′ cover |X| needs every point to lie in a minimal |Y|. This requires finiteness or well-foundedness of X̃, which is not stated.
The worry that the union defining |Y|°′ may contain Z not < Y is never resolved on this page. The argument sidesteps it via cover-plus-disjointness, which is valid given the tacit points above.

ideas.what: Axiomatic support map from abstract pieces to subsets of a point set, with open part |X| \ |∂X| and disjointness of interiors characterising |∘|
ideas.modern_name: Point-set realisation of an abstract cell or stratified structure; Stone-type recovery of points from a lattice of pieces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Regular CW complexes (Whitehead, Lundell–Weingram); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries); Grothendieck's own tame-topology programme
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 announces tame topology in general terms; this specific axiomatics appears unpublished

ideas.what: Closed cell = disjoint union of the open cells of its faces; the open part equals the closed cell minus the strictly smaller closed cells
ideas.modern_name: Cell decomposition / frontier condition for regular CW complexes or stratifications

ideas.what: The order on the elementary pieces equals inclusion of supports (face poset recovered from closures)
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of a regular CW complex / closure order of strata

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard verification inside an unpublished axiomatic set-up: open cells partition a closed cell, and the face order equals inclusion of closures. The broader 1986 Analysis situs axiomatics is little studied, but nothing on this page goes beyond classical cell-complex facts.
transcription_corrections: Page number at top is '34' (sequence 33, 34, 35), not '39'.
The displayed definition should read |Y|°′ =def |Y| \ ⋃_{Z∈X̃, |Z|⊊|Y|} |Z|, alongside the question |Y|° =? |Y|°′; the transcription garbles it as '|Z| def= |Y|°′'.
First line likely 'A-t-on même/encore, pour Y, Z ∈ X̃'; line 3 reads 'Ça ne semble pas contenu dans (i)(ii)(iii)(iv)'.
'Mais (ii bis) (en effet) nous dit que les |Y| recouvrent déjà |X| (et donc que les |Y|°′ recouvrent, les non vides)' is a better reading of the garbled lines.
In the final line, 'M' denotes Ỹ ∪ Z̃ (a reuse of the letter M, not the ambient set of pieces).
